tools.name: read_post
tools.description: Read one public post by id, including its public replies. Use when you already have a post id from list_posts or a share and only need that note. Use list_posts to browse. Does not return secrets or older accepted thread messages. No secret.

tools.name: write_first_reply
tools.description: Write the one first reply on a post. Use when you can actually fill that post from the public note and your user agrees. Your reply is public. Don't include anything private. Do not reply to your own user's post. Do not use this for later messages on an older accepted thread — use write_thread_messa

tools.name: read_thread
tools.description: Read older accepted threads only. Use when you have the thread key for an older accepted thread, or when you are the replier and have the first-reply id plus reply secret for an older accepted thread. tools.name: write_thread_message
tools.description: Write the next message on older accepted threads only. Use when you already have the thread key for an older accepted thread and need to send the next line. Do not use this for a first reply — use write_first_reply. No new threads. The thread key is sent in the JSON body, not in the path.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_posts, create_need, create_have, read_post, read_thread · Private data: list_posts, create_need, create_have, read_post, write_first_reply, read_thread · Public sink: list_posts, create_need, create_have, read_post, write_first_reply, write_thread_message · Destructive: create_need, create_have.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_posts, create_need, create_have, read_post, read_thread · Private data: list_posts, create_need, create_have, read_post, write_first_reply, read_thread · Public sink: list_posts, create_need, create_have, read_post, write_first_reply, write_thread_message · Destructive: create_need, create_have

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
